To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the conformational preferences and the optical rotation of the four β-amino alcohol derivatives studied in this work can be rationalized on the basis of the DFT calculations carried out in this work.
the optical rotation of the studied compounds is strongly affected by the conformational flexibility and the sign of optical rotation can be predicted with the aid of DFT calculations.

(1) the conformational flexibility is the main source of uncertainty in predicting the optical rotation of the carene β-amno alcohol; (2) the sign of the specific rotation can be predicted correctly by using DFT calculations, provided that the most stable conformations are used in the calculations; (3) the sign of specific rotation is mainly controlled by the relative energies of the most stable conformers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of novel, functionalized, and structurally diverse β‐amino alcohols and their application in the synthesis of biologically active compounds.
the synthesis of a series of novel chiral β-amino alchols based on the carene skeleton.
the synthesis and characterization of new compounds of the type 3, which have been prepared by a variety of methods and are of potential biological interest.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the DFT approach with B3LYP/aug-cc-pVDz is a very good method to study conformational properties of the studied carene β-ammo alcohols, while the calculated optical rotations can be useful for the qualitative prediction of the sign of the specific rotations, but not for the quantitative predictions of the magnitude of the specific rotation values.
the DFT method, in combination with the B3LYP hybrid functional and the aug-cc-pVXZ basis sets, provides a very good description of the studied systems.
, in general, DFT calculations are a very useful and reliable method for conformational analysis, and for the calculation of optical rotations of organic molecules.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are trying to understand the relationship of the chemical and physical properties of molecules to their structure and reactivity.

the B3LYP/6-31+G(d,p) level of theory is able to predict the sign of the specific rotation with a high degree of confidence, and that this level of theory is suitable for the study of conformational preferences of the studied compounds.
we have demonstrated the potential of using DFT methods for the prediction of the optical rotation of chiral molecules with a reasonable accuracy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the B3LYP/aug-cc-pVDz method is able to predict correctly the sign of optical rotations of carene β-amno alcohols.
the optical rotation of these compounds is strongly dependent on their conformations.
the B3LYP/6-31+G(d,p) level of theory is adequate for conformational analysis, but not for optical rotation calculations, of these types of systems.
